strategy.summary: Reproduce the complex-dtype bug in linalg.cond by building NumPy from the buggy commit b7e5173c13d1, applying the developer's test diff, and running the TestCond tests under pytest. The defect is decided by the dtype of the result, not its value. On the buggy revision test_cond_dtypes should fail for complex inputs with p in {1,-1,inf,-inf,'fro'} because the result is complex64 or complex128 instead of the real dtype. On the fixed revision (with result_t=_realType(result_t) in cond) all parametrized cases should pass. The Python 3.7.7 version in the issue is reporter-only and not documented, so it is not used as a pin.

system_packages: a C and C++ compiler toolchain
a Fortran compiler is not required by this revision as far as the evidence shows
build_commands: git clone https://github.com/numpy/numpy && cd numpy && git checkout b7e5173c13d1 && git submodule update --init
python -m pip install meson-python ninja Cython pytest hypothesis
pinned_because: numpy is the checkout under test and is not pinned to a version; the 1.19.1 and Python 3.7.7 in issue #18304 are reporter-observed, not a documented constraint, so they are not relied on
pytest and hypothesis are documented in README.md but carry no version constraint and are not numerically relevant, so latest compatible versions are used
Python version must be whatever the buggy revision's build metadata supports; that metadata is not in the evidence, so it is left null and must be checked in the checkout

strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision: test_cond_dtypes[csingle-1], [csingle-inf], [cdouble-1], [cdouble-inf] and the other complex cases with p in {1,-1,inf,-inf,'fro'} fail with an assert_equal dtype mismatch, because cond returns a complex dtype where get_real_dtype expects float32 or float64. The real-dtype cases (single, double) pass on both revisions. On the fixed revision (cond applies _realType to result_t): every test_cond_dtypes case passes, and test_basic_nonsvd with is_complex True and False passes. The transition from fail to pass on the test_cond_dtypes complex cases is the success criterion.
strategy.numerical_probe: Not needed. The oracle is the dtype equality on the fixed 3x3 real-valued matrix A cast to each dtype, so no random input or printed value is involved.

input_output_examples.expected_output: 253.11513101087314 as a real float (same value, real dtype)
126.26418916571008 as a real float (same value, real dtype)

risks: The provided test_command 'python -c import numpy; numpy.test()' is not a reliable selector: numpy.test was removed in NumPy 2.x and it runs the whole suite, so it is replaced with a targeted pytest node id
The buggy revision's own build requirements determine the usable Python version; Python 3.7.7 from the issue is not documented and very likely cannot build a current main checkout, so it is not used

The test relies on get_real_dtype and the single/double/csingle/cdouble aliases being importable in test_linalg.py; if the buggy revision's test module does not import them, the test errors on both revisions and gives no transition, so the import must be checked when applying the patch

The defect is not platform-specific or sanitiser-specific: it is a Python-level dtype selection in cond, so it should reproduce on any platform that builds NumPy; no architecture-only behaviour is evidenced

The complex scaling check in test_basic_nonsvd is value-based and assert_almost_equal may accept complex-vs-real equal values, so it may pass on the buggy revision; the dtype test is the one that carries the transition
Issue #18304 uses an unseeded random 10x10 matrix, so exact printed values are not reproducible; the dtype-only oracle avoids this
The reported fix is stated as landing in main and 2.3.x; behaviour in intermediate versions is not established by the evidence

oracle.reference_source: numpy/linalg/tests/test_linalg.py test_cond_dtypes from the PR diff
oracle.why: The check is dtype equality with get_real_dtype(dtype), which is exact and needs no numeric tolerance

strategy.fails_on_buggy: For complex dtypes with norm_ord in {1,-1,'fro',inf,-inf}, cond(A,p).dtype is complex, while assert_equal expects the real dtype, so an AssertionError is raised on the dtype mismatch.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: After result_t is downgraded to the real type via _realType, cond(A,p).dtype equals the real dtype for all dtype and norm_ord combinations, so all parametrized cases pass.
